subject: PulseCare throughput / latency pathway — hosted vs dedicated clarification
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 13 Jan 2028 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: PulseCare throughput / latency pathway — hosted vs dedicated clarification

Hi Asha —

Great to speak earlier. Quick recap of the engineering constraints you shared and the asks we promised to clarify: 

- Target steady-state throughput: ~400–600 qps for text generation (short prompts, avg 60 tokens output)
- P95 latency target: <= 120 ms for interactive UI flows; background batch work can accept higher latency
- Peak burst handling: up to 1k qps for 10–15s spikes (during scheduled events)
- Data residency: US-only, no on-prem requirement for Phase 1 but potential private VPC later in year 2

Immediate question for qualification: given the 120 ms p95 objective plus burst shape, would you be OK with a mixed approach (Hosted API for baseline + Dedicated reserved for sustained bursts), or do you prefer a single-mode commitment for predictability?

Attachments: I attached a short SLA/asks spreadsheet and your team’s network sketch you shared on the call (stubs below).

Next steps propose: 
1) If mixed: we (Marissa + Priyom) will sketch a runway plan showing expected unit cost and latency SLOs for a Hosted-first + Dedicated burst pool.
2) If Dedicated-only: we’ll produce a capacity estimate (GPU type, pool size, autoscale policy) and a baseline cost/commit schedule.

Can you confirm which path you want us to prioritize? If you want us to model both, we’ll do a concise 1-pager with cost and p95 estimates by Monday.

Thanks — enjoyed the conversation.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Asha Menon <asha.menon@pulsecare.io>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: PulseCare Infra <infra@pulsecare.io>
Date: Fri, 13 Jan 2028 11:06:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: PulseCare throughput / latency pathway — hosted vs dedicated clarification

Hi Karthik —

Thanks for the crisp recap — that matches our internal notes. A couple clarifications from our side: 

- The 120 ms p95 is a hard product requirement for the clinician-facing UI; even short missed windows cause UX friction.
- For the first quarter we want minimal ops overhead; leaning toward Hosted for speed to market, but we need a clear fallback if hosted p95 creeps beyond 120 ms during spikes.
- Security: SOC2 attestation is necessary; we’ll accept Hosted provided logs/audit hooks and data segmentation are available.
- Budget: we have flexible initial credits but will need an annual reserved-capacity quote for Year 1 planning should we choose Dedicated later.

Please prioritize modeling: (A) Hosted-first + Dedicated burst fallback, and (B) Dedicated-only (baseline + autoscale for bursts). If you can call out expected p95 under both assumptions for our traffic shape that would help.

Asha Menon
CTO, PulseCare
asha.menon@pulsecare.io

On attachments: I’m re-attaching the network sketch as a PNG for clarity.
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 15 Jan 2028 09:58:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: PulseCare throughput / latency pathway — hosted vs dedicated clarification

Karthik / Priyom — forwarding Asha’s confirmation. High-level engineering notes for the cost/perf model I’ll put together: 

- Traffic shape: steady 500 qps, 1k qps 15s spike every ~5 minutes (per their event sim); output tokens 60 avg.
- Hardware sensitivity: for these short-output workloads, A100-80GB-ish instances with 2–4 concurrent streams per GPU give best p95, but quantized LLM variants on T4s can reduce cost with modest p95 impact.
- Cache opportunities: we should estimate prefix KV cache hit assumptions (they said a lot of prompts are templated) — assume 15–25% hit to start.
- Fallback strategy: Hosted -> Dedicated pool with auto-failover by policy (route by latency SLO). Need to call out warm-up for KV caches on Dedicated.

I’ll run two scenarios and include a quick ops checklist (DNS routing, canary policy, cost delta). Priyom — can you draft a back-of-envelope reserved-capacity config (GPU type, nvlink layout, min pool size) so we can show numbers in the Monday deliverable?

Marissa
Director, Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Asha Menon <asha.menon@pulsecare.io>
Date: Mon, 15 Jan 2028 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: PulseCare throughput / latency pathway — hosted vs dedicated clarification

Asha / team —

Attaching preliminary config (summary below) — happy to expand.

Attachment stubs: PulseCare_SLA_asks.xlsx (sheet: latency_targets, traffic_profile)

Prelim Dedicated config (BOE):
- GPU type: 2 x L40s per node (balanced perf for throughput and burst)
- Min pool: 6 GPUs (3 nodes) to cover 500 qps steady at targeted p95 in tests
- Burst pool/autoscale: +6 GPUs on policy (scale target 1.8x sustained) to absorb 1k qps spikes; warm-up time 8–12s for KV loads
- Estimated p95: Dedicated baseline ~80–105 ms (depending on model quantization), Hosted baseline (with smart batching) ~95–140 ms — spikes can push hosted p95 > 200 ms without fallback
- Cost delta: Dedicated reserved model reduces unit cost by ~30% vs pure Hosted at the steady 500 qps point but has commit/ops tradeoffs

If that looks reasonable I’ll generate a short 1-pager with numeric cost tables and an ops checklist. Marissa — want me to include a quick note on KV cache pre-warming and suggested policies?

— Priyom
Priyom Das | Infra Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
